flags.headline: -7.72% to $8.96, giving back yesterday's guidance-optimism rally -- BTC-leverage/GAAP-loss thesis unchanged
flags.detail: MARA fell back to $8.96 (-7.72%), erasing most of yesterday's +5.54% guidance-optimism pop. Move is part of a broader, rate-driven retreat across the Bitcoin-miner-to-AI-infrastructure cohort (Cipher Mining -9%, TeraWulf -7%, HIVE -7%, Riot -4% -- Yahoo Finance/24-7 Wall St, 2026-08-19) as the 10-year Treasury yield sits near the top of its 52-week range, pressuring the group's long-duration, debt-financed data-center buildouts. No new company-specific news since the Q2 print. Underlying thesis unchanged: $611M Q2 net loss, 27% revenue miss, BTC mark-to-market volatility, $850M of convertible debt. Price targets from the guidance-optimism rally (Cantor $12, Clear Street $10) remain well below the $6-9 range the stock has traded in this week.
flags.thesis_link: Matches MARA key_risk: 'Persistent GAAP losses ($1.3B in Q1 2026 alone) driven by Bitcoin price volatility and mark-to-market accounting create existential risk if crypto enters a prolonged downturn and the company cannot service its $850M convertible debt obligations.'

evidence.source: Yahoo Finance / 24-7 Wall St (bitcoin-miner cohort, rate-driven)
MARA Q2 2026 earnings release (primary source, underlying thesis)

flags.headline: Aug-31 wildfire-reform deadline 12 days out, still no draft legislation -- shares calm/positive at +3.31%
flags.detail: No change to the core risk: as of this run, Edison still has not seen draft wildfire-liability-reform legislation, and the California legislative session ends Aug 31 -- 12 days out. California's complex regulatory and political environment creates uncertainty around cost recovery, rate base returns, and wildfire liability frameworks.'

flags.headline: Broad AI-infra/semis selloff on 30yr-yield highs + AI-debt jitters -- CRDO -13.2%, MRVL -7.8% the standouts, no company-specific news across the group
flags.detail: A closely watched semiconductor index (SOX) fell ~5% Tuesday 8/18 into today's continuation as the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield hit a fresh 19-year high and 'AI-debt-issuance anxiety' (Bloomberg's framing) pressured the whole premium-valuation AI/semis complex. Today's moves: CRDO -13.16% ($245.85, no CRDO-specific news found -- searches turned up no fresh downgrade or customer news, reads as high-beta amplification of the sector move given its 109x trailing P/E), MRVL -7.79% ($216.03, Evercore/Bloomberg attribute to rising-yield multiple compression ahead of its 8/27 print, not fundamentals), KEYS -5.52% (despite an actual Q3 beat + raised FY26 guidance reported 8/18 -- stock fell on the earnings day itself, pure multiple-compression on an otherwise strong print), TEL -5.82% (Evercore ISI issued a valuation-driven downgrade, explicitly citing 'how fully AI data center growth is already reflected' -- not a fundamentals call), CAT -4.60% (profit-taking after a strong print + record $72B backlog, dealer-inventory-reduction guidance cited as the specific concern, plus broad Asia weakness -- KOSPI -6%, Nikkei -2.8% -- overnight), LRCX -4.51%, AMD -4.30%, TSM -4.05%, ADI -3.49%, NXPI -1.73%, VST -3.85%, NVDA -2.39%. Every one of these names carries a near-identical 'premium valuation / multiple compression if AI capex moderates' key_risk in its screener report -- this reads as that generic valuation risk being priced, not any single thesis materializing. Not escalating to RED for any individual name absent company-specific bad news.
flags.thesis_link: Matches the shared valuation key_risk across CRDO, MRVL, KEYS, TEL, CAT, LRCX, AMD, TSM, ADI, NVDA (e.g. CRDO: 'Extreme valuation -- 109x trailing P/E... leaving minimal margin of safety for any execution miss or AI capex slowdown'). Multiple compression on rates, not an AI-capex-slowdown or execution-miss materializing.

evidence.source: Bloomberg (chip stocks hit as global bond anxiety builds)
StockTitan / FinancialContent (Keysight Q3 beat, raised guidance, stock fell)
Simply Wall St (Evercore ISI valuation-driven TEL downgrade)

flags.headline: Q3 beat on EPS and revenue, guidance reaffirmed, buyback raised -- resolves yesterday's earnings-watch flag positively
flags.detail: Toll Brothers reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $280.1M ($2.97/share, beating the $2.91 consensus) on $2.66B revenue (beat $2.61B consensus). Home sales gross margin compressed to 23.9% from 25.6% a year ago, and delivered homes fell to 2,662 from 2,959 -- a genuinely 'challenging market' per the CEO -- but full-year guidance was reaffirmed and the FY26 buyback target raised to $700M from $650M. Today's -1.99% price reaction reads as the same broad rate-driven macro pullback hitting premium names across the board (see the AI-infra/semis flag above), not a reaction to the print itself, which was solid.
